mainEntity.name: When should a product start a post-launch analytics engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Right after launch. The first 30 days generate the clearest behavioral signals your product will ever produce, so starting early costs far less than catching up later.

mainEntity.name: What metrics does the post-launch audit cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Day-one, day-seven, and day-30 retention rates, funnel completion, error frequency, session depth, feature adoption, and acquisition-to-activation conversion. Additional metrics get added based on your product category.

mainEntity.name: How long does a post-launch engagement typically run?

acceptedAnswer.text: At least three months. You need two full test-and-measure cycles to get reliable directional signals, and compounding improvements take sustained work to build.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with products built by other development teams?

acceptedAnswer.text: All the time. The audit works across any codebase or tech stack. A short onboarding session at the start gets the team fully up to speed.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between post-launch iteration and ongoing maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maintenance keeps things stable. Iteration moves your performance metrics forward. They serve different purposes, and the studio handles both within the same engagement when needed.

mainEntity.name: What does your A/B testing process involve?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each experiment runs with a single variable, a defined hypothesis, a calculated sample size, and a significance threshold that must be hit before any result counts.

mainEntity.name: Can the team help reprioritize a product roadmap based on post-launch data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. The initial roadmap almost always shifts after real users arrive. The audit surfaces which planned items still hold up and which assumptions the data has already contradicted.

mainEntity.name: Do you conduct user research as part of the engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In-app surveys, user interviews, and support ticket analysis run alongside behavioral data throughout, adding the interpretive context that analytics alone cannot provide. The role of UI/UX design in mobile app success becomes especially clear when qualitative feedback is compared with observed behavior.
Reports land biweekly at the close of each iteration cycle. They cover what moved, why it moved, and what gets prioritized next, with every metric tied to a defined target.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the product needs significant development work after the audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Development capacity is built into the Iterate and Accelerate tiers. If a Stabilize engagement surfaces bigger issues, the scope gets adjusted through business process automation and development support so nothing identified goes unresolved.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with early-stage products or only established ones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. Early-stage products benefit from strong analytics habits and MVP development, while established products often carry accumulated UX and technical debt that a structured audit quickly surfaces and prioritizes. Early-stage budgeting can also be benchmarked against typical MVP development cost before larger iteration cycles begin.

mainEntity.name: How do you get started with Inceptives Digital?

acceptedAnswer.text: Book a session with the team. The first conversation covers your product, its current performance, and exactly what a post-launch engagement would focus on and cost. Where discoverability is part of the issue, app store optimization and ASO, and effective marketing strategies for mobile apps can be included in the post-launch plan.
